newsitem.title: USA: Top U.S. negotiators to leave China talks - Post.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. negotiators to leave China talks - Post.

text.p: The U.S. government's two top trade negotiators with China plan to resign in early summer to spend more time with their families, the Washington Post reported Tuesday.

The two negotiators announced their plan to the Washington Post in response to queries by the newspaper about discussions they had held with their ex-boss, former U.S. trade representative Mickey Kantor, about joining Kantor's law firm in a new legal practice to represent U.S. companies seeking access to China and other Asian markets.

Lee Sands, the assistant trade representative for Japan and China, and his deputy, Deborah Lehr, are deeply involved in complex talks aims at opening the Chinese economy and getting Beijing to join the World Trade Organization.
